introduction.heading: Meaning and Framework of Partnership
introduction.details_en: Partnership is the relation between persons who have agreed to share profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all (Section 4, Indian Partnership Act, 1932).

key_definitions.explanation_en:
1. Agreement (Written or Oral)
2. Minimum 2, Maximum 50 members
3. Lawful business purpose
4. Profit-sharing objective
5. Mutual agency
6. Unlimited liability

When Partnership Deed is Silent:
• Profit/Loss: Equal sharing
• Interest on Capital: Not allowed
• Interest on Drawings: Not charged
• Salary/Commission: Not allowed
• Interest on Loan: 6% p.a. mandatory

practical_examples.title: Calculation of Interest on Capital
practical_examples.problem: Aryan's capital is Rs 60,000. Partnership deed provides 10% p.a. interest on capital. Calculate interest on capital for the year.
practical_examples.solution:
Interest = Capital * Rate of Interest
= 60,000 * (10 / 100) = Rs 6,000.

practical_examples.title: Interest on Capital with Time Adjustment
practical_examples.problem: Bhadresh introduced additional capital of Rs 40,000 on 1st October. Accounting year ends on 31st March. Rate of interest is 12% p.a. Calculate interest.
practical_examples.solution:
Period from 1st October to 31st March = 6 months.
Interest = 40,000 * (12 / 100) * (6 / 12) = Rs 2,400.

practical_examples.title: Interest on Drawings (Fixed Amount at Beginning of Month)
practical_examples.problem: Meera withdraws Rs 3,000 in the beginning of every month. Interest on drawings is 10% p.a. Find interest on drawings for the year.
practical_examples.solution:
Total annual drawings = 3,000 * 12 = Rs 36,000.
Formula for beginning of every month: n = 78 / 12.
Interest = 36,000 * (10 / 100) * (78 / 12) = Rs 2,340.

practical_examples.title: Interest on Drawings (Fixed Amount at End of Month)
practical_examples.problem: Jignesh withdraws Rs 4,000 at the end of every month. Interest on drawings is 12% p.a.
practical_examples.solution:
Total annual drawings = 4,000 * 12 = Rs 48,000.
Formula for end of every month: n = 66 / 12.
Interest = 48,000 * (12 / 100) * (66 / 12) = Rs 3,168.

practical_examples.title: Interest on Drawings (Fixed Amount in Middle of Month)
practical_examples.problem: Kavita withdraws Rs 5,000 in the middle of every month. Interest is 8% p.a.
practical_examples.solution:
Total annual drawings = 5,000 * 12 = Rs 60,000.
Formula for middle of every month: n = 72 / 12 (or 6 months flat).
Interest = 60,000 * (8 / 100) * (6 / 12) = Rs 2,400.

practical_examples.title: Manager's Commission Calculation (Before Charging)
practical_examples.problem: Net profit before manager's commission is Rs 60,000. Manager is entitled to 5% commission *before* charging such commission.

practical_examples.title: Manager's Commission Calculation (After Charging)
practical_examples.problem: Net profit before manager's commission is Rs 84,000. Manager is entitled to 10% commission *after* charging such commission.

practical_examples.title: Preparation of Profit and Loss Appropriation Account
practical_examples.problem: A and B are partners sharing profits in 2:1 ratio. Capitals are Rs 2,00,000 and Rs 1,00,000. Net profit is Rs 90,000. Interest on capital @ 9% p.a., Interest on drawings: A Rs 600, B Rs 400. A's salary Rs 8,000 per year. Prepare P&L Appropriation Account.
practical_examples.solution:
Credit Side: Net Profit Rs 90,000 + Int. on Drawings (A 600 + B 400) = Rs 91,000.
Debit Side: Int. on Capital (A 18,000 + B 9,000) = Rs 27,000; Salary (A) = Rs 8,000.
Total Debit = 35,000.
Divisible Profit = 91,000 - 35,000 = Rs 56,000.
Distributed to A (2/3) = Rs 37,333.33 and B (1/3) = Rs 18,666.67.

practical_examples.title: Partners' Capital Accounts (Fluctuating Method)
practical_examples.problem: Using data from Example 8, pass adjustment entries and show Fluctuating Capital Accounts for partners A and B.
practical_examples.solution: In Fluctuating Method, only one account (Capital Account) is maintained. Opening balances are credited. Interest on capital, salary, and profit share are credited. Drawings and interest on drawings are debited. Closing balances: A = Rs 2,55,933, B = Rs 1,27,067.

practical_examples.title: Partners' Capital and Current Accounts (Fixed Method)
practical_examples.problem: Using data from Example 8, maintain Capital and Current accounts under Fixed Capital Method.
practical_examples.solution: Capital accounts remain fixed at Rs 2,00,000 (A) and Rs 1,00,000 (B). All adjustments (interest, salary, drawings, profit shares) are channeled through Partners' Current Accounts.

practical_examples.title: Past Adjustments (Omission of Interest on Capital/Drawings)
practical_examples.problem: Profits for the year were distributed without providing 10% interest on capital (Capitals: X Rs 1,00,000, Y Rs 2,00,000). Pass a single adjustment entry.
practical_examples.solution:
Interest due: X = Rs 10,000, Y = Rs 20,000 (Total Rs 30,000 wrongly distributed as profit).
Net adjustment table shows X should be credited by Rs 5,000 and Y should be debited by Rs 5,000 (assuming equal profit sharing).
Journal Entry: Y's Capital/Current A/c Dr. Rs 5,000 To X's Capital/Current A/c Rs 5,000.

practical_examples.title: Correction of Omitted Salary and Commission
practical_examples.problem: Partner Z was entitled to a salary of Rs 12,000 per year, which was omitted before profit distribution. Show rectifying adjustment entry.
practical_examples.solution: Salary of Rs 12,000 reduces divisible profit, which lowers each partner's profit share. Rectifying entry passes the net impact directly through partners' current/capital accounts.

practical_examples.title: Guarantee of Minimum Profit to a Partner
practical_examples.problem: A, B and C share profits in 3:2:1 ratio. C is guaranteed a minimum profit of Rs 20,000. Total profit is Rs 90,000. Calculate final distribution.
practical_examples.solution:
Normal distribution: A = 45,000, B = 30,000, C = 15,000.
C faces a deficit of Rs 5,000 (20,000 - 15,000). This deficiency is borne by A and B in 3:2 ratio.
A contributes: 5,000 * 3/5 = Rs 3,000. B contributes: 5,000 * 2/5 = Rs 2,000.
Final Shares: A = Rs 42,000, B = Rs 28,000, C = Rs 20,000.

practical_examples.title: Guarantee by a Single Partner
practical_examples.problem: X and Y share profits 3:2. They admit Z with 1/6th share with a guarantee from X that Z's share will not be less than Rs 15,000. Total profit is Rs 60,000.
practical_examples.solution:
Z's calculated share = 60,000 * 1/6 = Rs 10,000. Deficit = Rs 5,000, which is entirely paid by X.
Final distribution: X = 36,000 - 5,000 = Rs 31,000; Y = Rs 24,000; Z = Rs 15,000.

practical_examples.title: Complex Profit Distribution with Loan Interest
practical_examples.problem: Partner P provided a loan of Rs 50,000 to the firm without any agreement. Net profit before loan interest is Rs 40,000. Show treatment.
practical_examples.solution:
As per Act, interest on partner's loan is 6% p.a. mandatory even if profit is low.
Interest = 50,000 * 6% = Rs 3,000 (charged to P&L Account).
Net Profit transferred to P&L Appropriation = 40,000 - 3,000 = Rs 37,000.

practical_examples.title: Comprehensive Final Illustration on Appropriation and Capital Accounts
practical_examples.problem: Comprehensive summary sum combining opening capitals, monthly drawings, interest rates, salaries, general reserves, and final divisible profit distribution for a 3-partner firm.
practical_examples.solution:
Step 1: Compute total interest on capitals and drawings.
Step 2: Debit P&L Appropriation with expenses, credit with net profit and drawings interest.
Step 3: Transfer final divisible profit to respective partner accounts according to the fixed or fluctuating capital method framework.

exercises.question: A partner withdraws Rs 4,000 at the beginning of every month. If interest on drawings is 10% p.a., calculate total interest on drawings for the year.
exercises.hint: Total annual drawings = 4,000 * 12 = 48,000. Period under beginning of every month formula = 78 / 12.

previous_years_questions.question: What is the rate of interest on a loan given by a partner when there is no partnership agreement?
previous_years_questions.solution: 6% per annum as per Section 16 of the Indian Partnership Act.

blocks.title: Expanding a Local Business: The Partnership Need
blocks.title_hi: स्थानीय व्यवसाय का विस्तार: साझेदारी की आवश्यकता
blocks.body: Imagine you own a famous bakery in Naroda, Ahmedabad. Demand is booming, but to open 3 new branches, you need ₹15 Lakhs capital and someone to manage logistics. You find a friend who has capital and operational skills.
blocks.body_hi: कल्पना कीजिए कि नरोदा, अहमदाबाद में आपकी एक प्रसिद्ध बेकरी है। मांग बढ़ रही है, लेकिन 3 नई शाखाएं खोलने के लिए आपको ₹15 लाख की पूंजी और रसद (लॉजिस्टिक्स) संभालने के लिए एक व्यक्ति की आवश्यकता है। आपको एक दोस्त मिलता है जिसके पास पूंजी और प्रबंधकीय कौशल दोनों हैं।
blocks.body_gu: ધારો કે નરોડા, અમદાવાદમાં તમારી એક પ્રખ્યાત બેકરી છે. માંગ ખૂબ વધી રહી છે, પરંતુ ૩ નવી શાખાઓ ખોલવા માટે તમને ₹૧૫ લાખની મૂડી અને સંચાલન માટે એક વ્યક્તિની જરૂર છે. તમને એક એવો મિત્ર મળે છે જેની પાસે મૂડી અને સંચાલન કૌશલ્ય બંને છે.
blocks.scenario: By joining hands, Rohan (the Baker) and Priya (the Manager) combine their resources to launch 'Royal Bakers'. But how do they share profits, losses, and responsibilities legally?
blocks.scenario_hi: एक साथ आकर, रोहन (बेकर) और प्रिया (प्रबंधक) 'रॉयल बेकर्स' शुरू करने के लिए अपने संसाधनों को मिलाते हैं। लेकिन वे कानूनी रूप से लाभ, हानि और जिम्मेदारियों को कैसे बांटेंगे?
blocks.scenario_gu: સાથે મળીને, રોહન (બેકર) અને પ્રિયા (મેનેજર) 'રોયલ બેકર્સ' શરૂ કરવા માટે તેમના સંસાધનોને એકત્રિત કરે છે. પરંતુ તેઓ કાયદાકીય રીતે નફો, નુકસાન અને જવાબદારીઓ કેવી રીતે વહેંચશે?

blocks.title: The Profit Dilemma
blocks.question: If Rohan works 12 hours daily at the bakery while Priya works 2 hours, but both invested equal capital and made no written agreement, how should a ₹3,000,000 yearly profit be divided?
blocks.question_hi: यदि रोहन बेकरी में प्रतिदिन 12 घंटे काम करता है जबकि प्रिया 2 घंटे काम करती है, लेकिन दोनों ने समान पूंजी लगाई है और कोई लिखित समझौता नहीं किया है, तो ₹3,00,000 का वार्षिक लाभ कैसे विभाजित होना चाहिए?
blocks.question_gu: જો રોહન બેકરીમાં દરરોજ ૧૨ કલાક કામ કરે છે જ્યારે પ્રિયા ૨ કલાક કામ કરે છે, પરંતુ બંનેએ સરખી મૂડી રોકી છે અને કોઈ લેખિત કરાર કર્યો નથી, તો ₹૩,૦૦,૦૦૦નો વાર્ષિક નફો કેવી રીતે વહેંચવો જોઈએ?
blocks.hint: Think: Does the law favor work hours or equal partnership status when there is no written contract?
blocks.hint_hi: सोचिए: जब कोई लिखित अनुबंध नहीं होता है, तो क्या कानून काम के घंटों का समर्थन करता है या समान साझेदारी का?
blocks.hint_gu: વિચારો: જ્યારે કોઈ લેખિત કરાર ન હોય, ત્યારે કાયદો કામના કલાકોને પ્રાધાન્ય આપે છે કે સરખા ભાગીદારીના અધિકારને?

blocks.title: Indian Partnership Act, 1932: Key Provisions
blocks.body:
According to Section 4 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, partnership is the relation between persons who have agreed to share profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all. In the absence of a Partnership Deed:
1. Profit/Loss is shared EQUALLY among partners.
2. No interest on capital or drawings is allowed/charged.
3. No salary, commission, or remuneration is payable to any partner.
4. Interest on loan given by a partner to the firm is payable @ 6% p.a.
blocks.body_hi:
भारतीय साझेदारी अधिनियम, 1932 की धारा 4 के अनुसार, साझेदारी उन व्यक्तियों के बीच का संबंध है जो सभी के द्वारा या उन सभी की ओर से काम करने वाले किसी एक व्यक्ति द्वारा चलाए जाने वाले व्यवसाय के लाभों को साझा करने के लिए सहमत हुए हैं। साझेदारी करार (Deed) के अभाव में:
1. लाभ/हानि सभी साझेदारों में समान रूप से बांटी जाती है।
2. पूंजी या आहरण पर कोई ब्याज नहीं दिया/लिया जाता।
3. किसी भी साझेदार को कोई वेतन, कमीशन या पारिश्रमिक नहीं दिया जाता।
4. साझेदार द्वारा फर्म को दिए गए ऋण पर 6% वार्षिक दर से ब्याज देय होता है।
blocks.body_gu:
ભારતીય ભાગીદારી કાયદા, ૧૯૩૨ની કલમ ૪ મુજબ, ભાગીદારી એ એવી વ્યક્તિઓ વચ્ચેનો સંબંધ છે જેઓ બધા દ્વારા અથવા બધા વતી તેમનામાંથી કોઈ એક દ્વારા ચલાવવામાં આવતા ધંધાનો નફો વહેંચવા માટે સંમત થયા હોય. ભાગીદારી કરારનામાની ગેરહાજરીમાં:
૧. નફો-નુકસાન સરખા હિસ્સે વહેંચાય છે.
૨. મૂડી પર વ્યાજ કે ઉપાડ પર વ્યાજ આપી/ગણી શકાતું નથી.
૩. કોઈ પણ ભાગીદારને પગાર, કમિશન કે મહેનતાણું આપી શકાતું નથી.
૪. ભાગીદારે પેઢીને આપેલ ધીરાણ/લોન પર વાર્ષિક ૬% લેખે વ્યાજ ચૂકવવું પડે છે.
blocks.key_takeaway: When there is no Partnership Deed, hard work or high capital does NOT grant extra profit share legally. Rules of 1932 Act automatically apply!
blocks.key_takeaway_hi: जब कोई साझेदारी विलेख नहीं होता है, तो कड़ी मेहनत या अधिक पूंजी कानूनी रूप से अतिरिक्त लाभ हिस्सा नहीं देती है। 1932 अधिनियम के नियम स्वतः लागू होते हैं!
blocks.key_takeaway_gu: જ્યારે ભાગીદારી કરારનામું ન હોય, ત્યારે સખત મહેનત કે વધુ મૂડી કાયદાકીય રીતે વધારાનો નફો મેળવવાનો હક આપતી નથી. ૧૯૩૨ના કાયદાના નિયમો આપમેળે લાગુ થાય છે!

blocks.title: Calculation of Interest on Drawings
blocks.problem: Partner Rohan withdraws ₹2,000 at the beginning of every month for personal use from Royal Bakers. The firm charges interest on drawings at 12% per annum. Calculate total interest on drawings for the year ending 31st March.
blocks.problem_hi: साझेदार रोहन रोयाय बेकर्स से व्यक्तिगत उपयोग के लिए प्रत्येक माह के प्रारंभ में ₹2,000 निकालता है। फर्म आहरण पर 12% प्रति वर्ष की दर से ब्याज लेती है। 31 मार्च को समाप्त होने वाले वर्ष के लिए आहरण पर कुल ब्याज की गणना करें।
blocks.problem_gu: ભાગીદાર રોહન રોયલ બેકર્સમાંથી અંગત વપરાશ માટે દર મહિનાની શરૂઆતમાં ₹૨,૦૦૦નો ઉપાડ કરે છે. પેઢી ઉપાડ પર વાર્ષિક ૧૨% લેખે વ્યાજ વસૂલે છે. ૩૧મી માર્ચે પૂરા થતા વર્ષ માટે ઉપાડ પર કુલ વ્યાજની ગણતરી કરો.

steps.explanation: Calculate total drawings made during the entire year.
steps.explanation_hi: पूरे वर्ष के दौरान किए गए कुल आहरण की गणना करें।
steps.explanation_gu: આખા વર્ષ દરમિયાન કરેલા કુલ ઉપાડની ગણતરી કરો.

steps.explanation: Determine the average time period (N) when amounts are withdrawn at the BEGINNING of every month. N = 78/12 years.
steps.explanation_hi: प्रत्येक माह के प्रारंभ में राशि निकालने पर औसत समय अवधि (N) निर्धारित करें। N = 78/12 वर्ष।
steps.explanation_gu: દર મહિનાની શરૂઆતમાં રકમ ઉપાડવામાં આવે ત્યારે સરેરાશ મુદત (N) નક્કી કરો. N = ૭૮/૧૨ વર્ષ.
સૂત્રનો ઉપયોગ કરો: વ્યાજ (I) = (P × R × N) / (૧૦૦ × ૧૨)

blocks.title: Why Charge Interest on Drawings?
blocks.title_hi: आहरण पर ब्याज क्यों लिया जाता है?
blocks.title_gu: ઉપાડ પર વ્યાજ શા માટે વસૂલવામાં આવે છે?
blocks.body: If one partner withdraws money frequently for personal use while another leaves their capital intact in the firm, the first partner is taking an unfair financial advantage. Charging Interest on Drawings deters unnecessary cash withdrawals and maintains financial fairness among partners!
blocks.body_hi: यदि एक साझेदार व्यक्तिगत उपयोग के लिए बार-बार पैसा निकालता है जबकि दूसरा अपनी पूंजी फर्म में छोड़ देता है, तो पहला साझेदार अनुचित वित्तीय लाभ उठा रहा है। आहरण पर ब्याज वसूलने से अनावश्यक नकद निकासी रुकती है और साझेदारों के बीच वित्तीय निष्पक्षता बनी रहती है!
blocks.body_gu: જો એક ભાગીદાર અંગત વપરાશ માટે વારંવાર પૈસા ઉપાડે છે જ્યારે બીજો ભાગીદાર પોતાની મૂડી પેઢીમાં રાખે છે, તો પહેલો ભાગીદાર ગેરવાજબી નાણાકીય ફાયદો ઉઠાવે છે. ઉપાડ પર વ્યાજ વસૂલવાથી બિનજરૂરી રોકડ ઉપાડ અટકે છે અને ભાગીદારો વચ્ચે નાણાકીય સમાનતા અને ન્યાય જળવાઈ રહે છે!

blocks.title: Knowledge Check: Partnership Provisions
blocks.question: In the absence of any written Partnership Deed, what interest rate is a partner entitled to receive on a loan extended to the firm?
blocks.question_hi: किसी लिखित साझेदारी विलेख के अभाव में, किसी साझेदार को फर्म को दिए गए ऋण पर किस ब्याज दर को प्राप्त करने का अधिकार है?
blocks.question_gu: કોઈપણ લેખિત ભાગીદારી કરારનામાની ગેરહાજરીમાં, ભાગીદારે પેઢીને આપેલ લોન પર કેટલા ટકા વ્યાજ મેળવવાનો હક છે?
blocks.explanation: According to the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, if there is no partnership deed, a partner is entitled to interest at 6% p.a. on any advance/loan given to the firm beyond their capital contribution.
blocks.explanation_hi: भारतीय साझेदारी अधिनियम, 1932 के अनुसार, यदि कोई साझेदारी विलेख नहीं है, तो साझेदार अपने पूंजी योगदान से परे फर्म को दिए गए किसी भी अग्रिम/ऋण पर 6% प्रति वर्ष की दर से ब्याज पाने का हकदार है।
blocks.explanation_gu: ભારતીય ભાગીદારી કાયદા, ૧૯૩૨ મુજબ, જો ભાગીદારી કરારનામું ન હોય, તો ભાગીદારે પેઢીને આપેલ વધારાની લોન/ધીરાણ પર વાર્ષિક ૬% લેખે વ્યાજ મેળવવાનો કાયદાકીય હક છે.
